title: Asia stocks fall as Alphabet, Samsung results disappoint; more tech earnings loom
full_text:
Investing.com-- Asian stocks fell on Thursday, surrendering early gains as disappointing results from Alphabet and a sell-off in Samsung Electronics weighed on technology shares, while investors awaited earnings from Amazon and Intel for further clues on the outlook for artificial intelligence investment.
U.S. stock index futures also fell in Asian trading Thursday, with Nasdaq 100 Futures sliding 1.5%. Wall Street ended slightly higher overnight.
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) shares slumped about 10% in after-hours U.S. trading after the company reported results that fell short of expectations and signalled heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), by contrast, gained about 3% after its results showed stronger-than-expected cash flow, highlighting investors' growing focus on whether technology companies can generate sufficient returns to justify their substantial AI investments.
Get premium stock market insights with InvestingPro subscription
S.Korea's KOSPI retreats on Samsung profit miss
South Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 3%. Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) shares fell nearly 6% despite the company reporting record third-quarter earnings, as investors focused on a miss in semiconductor profit expectations and uncertainty over additional shareholder returns.
Investors were also disappointed that Samsung did not provide immediate details of additional shareholder returns, with the company saying it would finalise its next policy in January. Its mobile business recorded an operating loss of 800 billion won as higher memory costs squeezed profitability.
Samsung warned that AI-driven memory demand would outstrip industry supply in 2027 and projected semiconductor capital expenditure of 76.8 trillion won this year, up 62% from 2025.
The decline followed a rally of nearly 7% in the KOSPI on Wednesday, when SK Hynix (KS:000660) surged 11% after reporting a stronger-than-expected profit and announcing a 100 trillion won ($75 billion) shareholder-return plan. SK Hynix shares rose a further 1.6% on Thursday.
Elsewhere, China's Shanghai Composite fell 1.2% and the blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index slipped 1.2%, with chip stocks leading losses.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng traded largely flat, although its Hang Seng TECH sub-index slid 2%.
Japan's Nikkei 225 edged 0.2% higher after erasing most of its gains, while the broader TOPIX index fell 0.3%.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.4%, while Singapore's Straits Times Index edged up 0.1%.
Futures tied to India's Nifty 50 fell 0.3%.
Fed holds steady; BOJ decision awaited
Investors were also preparing for the Bank of Japan's policy decision on Friday, after its two-day meeting began on Thursday.
The central bank is widely expected to keep its policy rate at 1.25%, following a rate increase in September, while potentially raising its inflation forecasts as higher oil prices and a weak yen add to price pressures.
Markets will scrutinise Governor Kazuo Ueda's comments for clues on whether the BOJ could raise rates again as soon as December.
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, although two policymakers voted in favour of a rate increase.
Markets were pricing in roughly a 78% chance of a U.S. rate increase in December, according to CME FedWatch, leaving investors sensitive to incoming inflation data. September's U.S. personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is due on Friday.
Attention later shifts to Amazon and Intel, whose results and guidance will help investors assess whether strong AI demand can sustain the enormous spending on data centres, chips and cloud infrastructure.

title: Samsung posts record Q3 earnings; shares slide as net profit misses estimates
full_text:
Investing.com-- Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) reported record quarterly revenue and operating profit on Thursday, as booming demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure drove earnings at its memory chip business to new highs.
But shares of the South Korean giant slid 6% as its net profit missed expectations by a wide margin on surging costs and continued losses in its mobile unit.
Get real-time earnings updates with InvestingPro subscription -- at 55% off now
The South Korean technology giant posted operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.5 billion) for the July-September quarter, up 783% from a year earlier and 20% from the previous quarter.
Revenue rose 127% year-on-year to 195.3 trillion won, while net profit increased to 75.1 trillion won from 12.2 trillion won a year earlier.
But net profit missed Bloomberg estimates of 89.06 trillion won. Net profit was pressured chiefly by a 9.5 trillion won loss on financing and income.
Samsung’s semiconductor division was the biggest driver of its quarterly earnings, with operating profit from the division at 106.5 trillion won. But the print also fell slightly short of Bloomberg estimates of 108.45 trillion won.
A slowdown in cash flows from operating activities-- to 98.6 trillion won in Q3 from 105.1 trillion won in Q2-- was also a point of concern, given that Samsung’s shareholder return plans are closely tied to its cash levels.
Samsung outlined shareholder returns of 30 trillion won for the third quarter-- through an ordinary and preferred share dividend of 4,601 won. The company had pledged to return between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won to shareholders in 2026, and has so far planned or completed about 35 trillion won in returns.
The return of the remaining 55 trillion and 75 trillion won to investors will consist of a "substantial share repurchase and cancellation program, along with cash dividends," Samsung said, and will be outlined in a late-January board meeting.
Mobile business logs operating loss, 2026 capex to grow sharply
Samsung’s Device eXperience division, which covers its mobile, home appliances, and electronics sales, logged an operating loss of 800 billion won in Q3, compared to a 3.5 trillion won profit from a year ago and a 800 billion won loss in the second quarter.
The unit was pressured chiefly by soaring memory and electronic component costs, spurred largely by supply tightness stemming from AI-driven demand.
The weak mobile unit print, coupled with sluggish growth in Samsung’s display and acoustics units, also raised questions over the health of the company beyond its standout memory chip business.
Samsung forecast 2026 capital expenditures of 84.4 trillion won, up sharply from 52.8 trillion won in 2025, as the company scaled up its production capacity to meet increasing memory demand.
The higher capex forecast comes amid growing scrutiny of the AI investment cycle, and whether the billions of dollars poured into the technology will yield adequate returns.
Samsung’s Q3 earnings come just a day after rival SK Hynix Inc (KS:000660) clocked record top and bottom-line prints for the same period, and pledged total shareholder returns of 100 trillion won for 2026.
SK Hynix shares rose 0.9% on Thursday.
Samsung said AI investment is likely to continue supporting memory demand in the fourth quarter, particularly for products used in new central processing unit and graphics processing unit platforms. Demand for high-density quad-level cell SSDs is also rising as personal AI agent services expand.
Samsung’s memory sales rose 427% from a year earlier to 140.7 trillion won, as the company significantly expanded sales of high-bandwidth memory (HBM4) and met growing demand for server solid-state drives (SSDs).
Ayushman Ojha contributed reporting

title: BOJ preview October: hawkish hold expected as inflation remains sticky
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Bank of Japan is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged at the conclusion of a two-day meeting on October 30, although the central bank is expected to maintain a hawkish bias amid increasingly sticky Japanese inflation.
The BOJ is expected to leave its benchmark rate at 1.25%, after raising the rate by 50 basis points so far this year.
The central bank had during its September meeting signaled that it will continue to consider more rate hikes, with Japanese inflation seen moving closer towards its 2% annual target.
Core consumer price index inflation rose to 2.1% in September, while underlying inflation rose to 2.4%.
Japanese consumer inflation has steadily increased this year despite government subsidies on fuel and utilities, as rising energy and raw material costs factored into higher producer price index inflation.
Recent reports said Japan is also planning to end its fuel subsidies by December– a move that could spur a sharp upward correction in inflation.
Against this backdrop, the BOJ is broadly expected to maintain its hawkish bias. But uncertainty over the Japanese economy, amid growing headwinds from the Middle East conflict, is expected to temper just how aggressively the BOJ can hike rates in the coming months.
“We forecast the BoJ will raise interest rates 25bp in December and follow that with another 25bp hike in March next year,” ANZ analysts said in a note.
“The BoJ must also keep a watchful eye on growth developments… Amid elevated geopolitical uncertainty the growth backdrop has been uneven this year and does not warrant aggressive tightening,” ANZ analysts said.
BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda had signaled in September that the BOJ will remain on guard to raise rates further in the face of sticky inflation.
The BOJ has raised rates by a cumulative 1.35% since early-2024, after it ended over a decade of ultra-loose policy.
Prior to the BOJ’s decision, Tokyo CPI inflation for October is also due on Friday, and is likely to factor into future rate decisions by the central bank.
How will the Nikkei 225 react?
Japan’s Nikkei 225 benchmark logged wild swings in the run-up to Friday’s decision, hit chiefly by volatility in technology shares.
Any hawkish comments from the BOJ are likely to further rattle tech valuations, given their sensitivity to interest rates. A stronger yen could also dent exporters, which make up a large portion of the Nikkei.
But higher rates stand to benefit lenders and domestically-exposed sectors. Japan’s major banks have benefited greatly from rising domestic interest rates.
How will USDJPY react?
The Japanese yen has usually responded favorably to hawkish signals from the BOJ, with the USD/JPY pair– which gauges the amount of yen required to purchase one dollar– likely to fall.
The BOJ’s recent monetary tightening has also been motivated by a weak yen, with the central bank concerned that a soft yen could drive up import costs and further underpin inflation.
Japan and the U.S. had engaged in an unprecedented, joint intervention operation in August to support the laggard currency. But USDJPY has since recouped a bulk of its losses.

title: Oil dips as traders weigh Iran diplomacy against renewed strike risks
full_text:
Investing.com-- Oil prices dipped in Asian trading on Thursday as investors assessed fresh diplomatic efforts to contain the conflict in the Middle East, although concerns about renewed U.S. military strikes on Iran and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure continued to underpin prices near six-month highs.
As of 20:18 ET (00:18 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in December fell 0.8% to $114.41 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also slipped 0.8% to $101.99 per barrel.
Both contracts had risen in the previous session after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement said it had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery.
Get premium commodity market insights with InvestingPro -- at 55% off now
The market remained caught between hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough and fears that a renewed escalation could further disrupt oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global crude shipments.
The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's top security body, in a move that could help establish a channel for negotiations.
Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump told Axios on Wednesday that negotiations were taking place through mediators, but stressed that he did not know whether they would produce results.
Qatari mediators have presented Tehran with a new draft proposal aimed at ending the conflict. However, an Iranian official described the ideas as unacceptable, Reuters reported.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have also held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran this week.
Trump has raised the prospect of renewed military action against Iran after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, while Washington has warned regional allies to prepare for possible strikes and Iranian retaliation against energy facilities.
The risk of further attacks has become a key driver of oil prices, with the conflict threatening both production facilities and shipping routes. Prolonged disruptions to traffic through the Strait of Hormuz could sharply tighten global supply, while attacks on Saudi infrastructure could limit the kingdom's ability to export crude.
U.S. inventory data provided some additional support. Commercial crude stocks fell by 1.9 million barrels to 410.6 million barrels in the week ended Oct. 23, according to the Energy Information Administration, compared with analysts' expectations for a small increase.
However, the inventory report offered a mixed picture of fuel demand. Gasoline stocks rose by 3.9 million barrels, defying expectations for a decline, while distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, fell by 1.5 million barrels.

title: Gold slips after Fed holds rates, PCE inflation data in focus
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices fell on Wednesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve held interest rates steady but offered limited clarity on its next move, leaving investors uncertain about the prospect of further tightening before year-end as they awaited fresh inflation data.
At 21:12 ET (01:12 GMT), XAU/USD fell 0.4% to $4,051.91 an ounce, while Gold Futures gained 0.3% to $4,063.65. XAG/USD rose modestly to $54.0410 an ounce, while XPT/USD slipped marginally to $1,540.26. XPD/USD advanced 0.8% to $1,024.13, while the U.S. dollar Index edged up to 102.22.
Spot gold fell after posting modest gains for three consecutive sessions. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged, a decision markets had largely anticipated.
However, Chair Kevin Warsh said the Fed could reduce its scheduled policy decisions from eight to six annually starting next fall.
Traders continue to anticipate a rate increase in December as persistently high energy prices complicate efforts to bring inflation under control.
Investors will look to Thursday's September personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, for further clues on the likely direction of rates before year-end.
Gold also remains vulnerable to broader equity-market selloffs as investors assess whether heavy artificial intelligence spending is weighing on corporate cash flow.
Last week's AI-driven stock rout prompted some investors to sell gold to cover losses elsewhere, helping push bullion to its lowest level since July. Gold has fallen 2.5% in October and is on track for a second consecutive monthly decline.
Central-bank buying remains an important source of longer-term support. Goldman Sachs estimates that central banks purchased 79 tonnes of gold in August, nearly five times the average monthly volume before 2022, with China accounting for 25 tonnes.
Rick Kanda, managing director of The Gold Bullion Company, said sustained central-bank demand could help gold appreciate over time or at least provide a firm price floor.
He noted that central-bank purchases add to demand alongside interest rates, investor confidence and geopolitical uncertainty. "However, sustained central bank demand could nevertheless help maintain prices over the long term.”

title: Phillips 66 posts record quarterly profit on refining strength
full_text:
By Nicole Jao
NEW YORK, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Phillips 66 on Wednesday reported a record quarterly profit, topping Wall Street estimates, powered by higher refining margins on fuel supply disruptions due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
US fuelmakers benefited from historically wide refining margins as global fuel supplies have tightened and inventories have depleted on a war-related supply crunch in both the Middle East and Russia. Prices for diesel, which underpins everything from manufacturing to agriculture, have hit record highs, creating pain for consumers and US President Donald Trump’s Republican party, but a boon for refiners.
Peers Valero Energy and HF Sinclair also posted record third-quarter profits as US refiners emerged as key beneficiaries of the disruptions that tightened global supplies, while refinery utilization remained at multi-year highs.
Shares of the Houston-based refiner rose 1.32%.
STRONG DISTILLATES YIELDS, FREIGHT TAILWINDS
The combination of strong distillate margins and favorable freight positioning improved the Houston-based refiner’s ability to capture value in the refining segment, executives said during a call with investors on Wednesday.
Realized margins in the third quarter was $38 per barrel, up from $24.08 per barrel in the previous quarter.
"As we stay in this strong distillate economy, and our kit is really tuned to take advantage of that distillate production. I see the market capture favorable for all regions that we operate in," Brian Mandell, executive vice president of marketing and commercial, said on Wednesday.
The company posted record distillate yield of 41% in the third quarter.
The refiner locked in more than 40 time-chartered vessels before freight markets tightened and has another 40 ships scheduled to join its fleet over the next two-and-a-half years at rates below current market levels, Mandell said. That gave the company a cost advantage as tanker rates climbed, helping offset higher transportation costs faced by other market participants.
Higher freight rates have squeezed some crude and product traders that export to Europe and Asia.
Phillips 66 reported an adjusted profit of $14.08 per share for the three months ended September 30, compared with analysts’ average estimate of $11.73, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Net income rose to $5.62 billion from $133 million a year earlier, marking its highest quarterly profit on record.
Adjusted earnings at its renewable fuel segment rose to $191 million during the quarter, compared to a loss of $43 million a year earlier.
Phillips 66 said its Coastal Bend expansion project remains on track, with initial volumes expected in the fourth quarter and full ramp-up to 350,000 barrels per day in early 2027, improving transportation between Permian and Eagle Ford output and NGL processing plants in Corpus Christi and Sweeny in Texas.
In August, the company, Kinder Morgan and HF Sinclair said they would proceed with the proposed $5 billion Western Gateway Pipeline system and had finalized a joint venture agreement.

title: Bloomberg, 2 trading firms subscribe to faster access to Trump posts- Reuters
full_text:
Investing.com-- Truth Social– a social media platform founded by U.S. President Donald Trump– has signed on Bloomberg and two Wall Street firms for faster access to the president’s posts, Reuters reported on Wednesday.
The two firms are Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, Reuters reported, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter.
The service, for which Truth Social charges up to $100,000 a month, gives users faster access to Trump’s posts on the social media site.
His posts are known to cause wild swings in financial markets, with the service potentially giving subscribers a clear advantage over everyday investors.
Trump Media & Technology Group Corp (NASDAQ:DJT), which runs Truth Social, had unveiled the service in July, pitching it to news and trading firms. But the service was criticized for being unethical on the grounds that Trump was selling paid access to his statements as a sitting president.
Trump Media had in August told investors it had signed more than 10 customers for the service.

title: Argentina sees EU soymeal opportunity as deforestation rules threaten Brazil trade
full_text:
(Adds full name and title of Mauricio Buffon in paragraph 9)
By Maximilian Heath and Oliver Griffin
BUENOS AIRES/SAO PAULO, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Brazil’s soybean industry fears the European Union’s new anti-deforestation regulations (EUDR) could curb soymeal exports to the bloc, creating an opening for rival supplier Argentina, which says it is better placed to comply with the incoming rules.
Brazil is the EU’s largest supplier of soybean meal for animal feed, accounting for about half of the bloc’s imports last year, according to data from the European Feed Manufacturers’ Federation (FEFAC). Brazil exported a record 23.3 million metric tons of soymeal in 2025.
Starting December 30, the EUDR will require importers to prove their products are not linked to deforested land, with significant penalties for non-compliance.
In Brazil, extensive farmland across central and northeastern states has been developed in cleared ecosystems in recent decades, whereas Argentina’s most important farmlands are spread across the vast Pampas plains, where farmers have been producing for over a century.
The EUDR is raising alarm in Brazil’s agriculture sector, with FEFAC warning that traceability requirements under the rules could shut out up to 4 million tons of soymeal, roughly 17% of total exports.
According to FEFAC’s latest report on how anti-deforestation rules may impact supply chains, Brazil was assigned a "medium" risk rating, with the west-central state of Mato Grosso and others facing "structural and logistical hurdles" that could restrict the expansion of fully EUDR-compliant supply chains.
Dante Romano, research manager at Rosario-based grains broker Max Agro, explained that farmers in central Brazil are more than 2,000 kilometres away from sea ports and often have to change between trucks, barges and trains to get their grains to export terminals, making supply chains difficult to trace.
Argentina’s prime soy-producing lands are no more than 350 kilometres away from the Rosario port hub, making traceability considerably easier, and cheaper.
For Mauricio Buffon, president of industry association Aprosoja, the landmark legislation unfairly targets Brazil. He said environmental restoration efforts were underway in some regions even as new cropland was being developed.
"Brazil’s environmental problems are much smaller than the size of our agriculture," the Aprosoja president said.
The EUDR will come into effect just days before Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva inaugurates a new term as president of Brazil, after beating right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who had said he would free production from "environmental hurdles" and let farmers do "whatever they wished" on their lands.
’ARGENTINA IS READY’
Further south, Argentina’s powerful soybean crushing industry is positioning itself to benefit from any disruption faced by Brazilian exporters in meeting the EU’s tougher rules.
"We can easily fill that gap," said Gustavo Idigoras, president of Argentina’s CIARA-CEC grains exporters and crushers chamber, referring to potential export losses in Brazil, which he estimated at 5 million to 6 million tons.
"Argentina is ready," Idigoras said, pointing to the country’s VISEC traceability system, which tracks soybeans and beef from production through to export and is fully operational.
In its latest risk assessment, FEFAC assigned Argentina a "low" risk rating for EUDR-related supply disruptions, projecting that nearly all of the country’s soymeal crop in the first half of 2027 would meet requirements.
Romano said Argentina could capitalize on any shortfalls in Brazilian shipments. At the same time, he said, Brazil may seek to expand sales to alternative markets as Argentine exporters divert more volumes to meet European demand.
Argentina is the world’s largest soymeal exporter, shipping about 27 million metric tons last year, roughly a quarter of which went to Southeast Asia.
The adjustments come at a sensitive moment in relations between the EU and Mercosur, after the bloc and the South American trade group reached a provisional free-trade agreement in May following decades of negotiations.
Argentina and Brazil are both members of Mercosur along with Uruguay and Paraguay, another key supplier of soybeans to Argentina’s crushing industry.
Paraguay’s CAPPRO grains crushing chamber said the country has "favorable structural conditions" to meet European requirements. In its Region Oriental, where most soybeans are grown, legislation passed in 2004 prohibits deforestation for agricultural use.
Like Argentina, Paraguay received a low risk rating from FEFAC.

title: Vietnam sets 65% state ownership floor for major banks, to retain control of strategic groups
full_text:
HANOI, Oct 29 (Reuters) - Vietnam has approved a plan to set the minimum state ownership level for state-run lenders at 65% by 2030, part of a broader programme to restructure state capital in major enterprises and banks.
The restructuring plan, released late on Wednesday, covers 21 state-owned and state-backed enterprises, and forms part of Vietnam’s 2026-2030 programme to restructure state capital, with the aim of preserving state control in strategic sectors while giving authorities the flexibility to adjust their holdings in selected companies and lenders.
• The state plans to retain shares of at least 65% in BIDV, Vietcombank and VietinBank by 2030. The government’s stakes currently stand at 76.73% in BIDV and 74.80% in Vietcombank, above the new 65% threshold, while its holding in VietinBank is 64.46%
• The decision did not specify which mechanism would be used to reach those ownership levels or whether any stake sales, placements or capital raising will be undertaken
• The plan also maintains 100% state ownership in Agribank through 2030, making it the only bank among those covered that will remain fully state-owned
• The state will maintain 100% state ownership through 2030 in other major strategic enterprises, including Vietnam Electricity (EVN), the Vietnam National Industry-Energy Group (PetroVietnam), the Vietnam Expressway Corporation (VEC)
• Under the plan, the state’s direct holding in Vietnam Airlines is set to rise to 86.42% by 2030 from the current level of 39.29%
• The state-owned investor, the State Capital Investment Corporation, already holds a stake of about 47% in the airline, according to LSEG data
• The plan also envisages a reduction in the state’s stake in Vietnam Rubber Group to 75% from 96.77%, maintaining its majority control
• Vietnam had 695 state-owned enterprises by the end of 2025, including 497 wholly owned by the government, local media reported

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority leaves interest rates unchanged, tracking Fed move
full_text:
HONG KONG, Oct 29 (Reuters) - The Hong Kong Monetary Authority left its base interest rate unchanged on Thursday at 4.25%, following the US Federal Reserve’s decision to hold rates steady.
Hong Kong’s monetary policy moves in lock-step with the United States as the city’s currency is pegged to the greenback in a tight range of 7.75-7.85 per dollar.
"US interest rate adjustments are subject to considerable uncertainty, and will depend on developments in inflation, labour market, and other economic data, and may influence the interest rate environment in Hong Kong," HKMA said in a statement.
The outlook for the Hong Kong dollar and interbank rates can vary due to various factors, such as the market’s risk appetite for carry trades, and the supply-demand conditions for Hong Kong dollars which are, in turn, influenced by capital market activities and other seasonal factors, it added.

title: U.S. stock futures drop as Alphabet slides on soft earnings, Microsoft firms
full_text:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures fell early-Thursday, pressured chiefly by a sharp drop in Google owner Alphabet after its third-quarter earnings missed expectations.
Middling earnings from memory chip giant Samsung also weighed, with the stock falling sharply in Seoul trade and triggering losses across the broader chipmaking sector.
Alphabet’s drop largely overshadowed gains in Microsoft after its quarterly earnings beat expectations. Markets also parsed comments from the Federal Reserve that could herald more interest rate hikes in the coming months.
Nasdaq 100 Futures slid 1.1% to 29,647.75 points by 02:43 ET (06:43 GMT). S&P 500 Futures fell 0.3% to 7,760.0 points, and Dow Jones Futures rose 0.4% to 52,899.0 points.
Futures fell after a mildly positive session on Wall Street, where blowout third-quarter earnings from memory chip giant SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) helped spur some gains in tech.

Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) was among the worst aftermarket performers on Wednesday evening, losing 9.8% after its third-quarter profit missed expectations by a wide margin.
While its revenue just edged past expectations on growing returns from its cloud unit, overall profitability was impacted by continued, outsized spending on artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure.
The earnings release added to growing Wall Street concerns over whether the billions of dollars poured into AI in recent years will be able to generate adequate returns– a notion that battered tech stocks since late-September.
Investors also largely looked past Google’s unveiling of a new AI model– Gemini 4 Carbon.
Samsung (KS:005930) added to concerns over stretched AI spending, with the company’s bottom line missing expectations as it forecast more capital spending in the coming year.
Samsung’s mobile unit division clocked a second straight quarter of losses, adding to uncertainty over the impact of soaring component prices on consumer electronics.
On the other hand, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) rose 2.7% in aftermarket trade after it delivered a top and bottom-line beat in its fiscal first-quarter earnings.
Microsoft’s Azure unit grew more than expected in the quarter, indicating that the tech giant was progressing well in its efforts to monetize AI.
Alphabet and Microsoft are among the largest spenders on AI infrastructure– a group dubbed as Wall Street’s “hyperscalers,” with their earnings offering the most insight into the AI trade and returns from the fast-growing technology.
Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), another hyperscaler, is set to report September quarter earnings on Thursday.
Fed leaves rates on hold, Warsh offers few direct cues
Wall Street ended slightly higher on Wednesday after the Fed left interest rates unchanged at 4.0% as widely expected, with two of the 12-member Federal Open Market Committee calling for a 25 basis point hike.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking after the meeting, highlighted recent strength in the economy, but declined to provide any forward guidance on interest rates.
Still, he reiterated the central bank’s commitment to its 2% annual inflation target. The Fed had raised rates by 25 basis points in September, as it moved to cool increasingly sticky inflation.
Warsh’s comments on the economy– where he highlighted resilient spending and stable employment– were largely interpreted as hawkish, with Treasury yields rising sharply on his comments.
The 10-year yield rose back above 5% after Warsh’s address, although it did trim some gains in evening trade.
Markets were also seen ratcheting up bets on a 25 bps hike by the Fed in December, with CME Fedwatch indicating a 81.8% chance for a hike– up from 75.1% a week earlier.
Focus now turns to upcoming third-quarter gross domestic product data and PCE price index data for September– both of which are likely to factor into the Fed’s plans for interest rates.
Core PCE data is the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, and is expected to have remained well above the central bank’s 2% annual target in September.

title: Vance reaches out to Iran security official on peace talks- WSJ
full_text:
Investing.com-- U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, to revive peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
President Trump told reporters Wednesday evening that he approved Vance’s outreach, stating that they "need help with medical supplies and various things."
Last week, Trump said the administration was not in talks with Iran and suggested military action could be coming after the midterm elections.
Get more breaking news on U.S.-Iran talks and oil prices by subscribing to InvestingPro
Vance’s letter and follow-up discussions between U.S. and Iranian officials have not included specific peace proposals, the WSJ report said. The talks have instead centered on a possible framework for negotiations.
Rezaei said last week that Iran would not negotiate with Washington until certain core demands were met, specifically lifting a naval blockade against the country, unfreezing some foreign assets, and ending all military action against Tehran.
A memorandum of understanding reached in June fell apart two weeks after it was signed due to conflicting interpretations on how to unlock shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Hormuz has remained largely closed, with Iran also seen increasing attacks on shipping through the waterway in recent weeks.

title: OMV profit jumps 68% but misses estimates as refining margins soar
full_text:
Investing.com -- OMV AG (VIE:OMVV) reported its strongest quarterly operating result since late 2022 on Thursday, as soaring refining margins and higher oil and gas prices boosted earnings, although the Austrian energy group fell short of analyst expectations. The company also raised its full-year price outlook and increased planned investment.
OMV's clean CCS operating result rose 68% year on year to €2.12 billion in the third quarter, below the €2.17 billion consensus compiled by Vara. Clean CCS net income attributable nearly doubled to €1.15 billion, while revenue from continuing operations climbed 43% to €8.96 billion.
The improvement was led by the Fuels business, where clean CCS operating profit surged to €1.12 billion from €413 million a year earlier. OMV's European refining indicator margin more than tripled to $37.50 per barrel from $11.54, supported by tight supplies of refined products amid the Middle East conflict and the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Refinery utilisation in Europe reached 92%.
Energy segment operating profit increased 51% to €936 million, reflecting higher realised oil and gas prices. However, hydrocarbon sales volumes fell 26% to 225,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, as the conflict disrupted liftings in the Middle East.
Chemicals operating profit declined to €63 million from €222 million, reflecting weaker market conditions for Borouge International.
Chief Executive Emma Delaney said Fuels and Energy were the main earnings drivers, while Chemicals contributed less. She added that the group remained focused on safe, reliable operations and disciplined project execution amid geopolitical challenges.
OMV raised its 2026 Brent price assumption to above $95 per barrel, from a previous range of $85 to $95, and now expects its average realised gas price to reach around €45 per megawatt-hour, up from €40. Its European refining margin assumption increased to around $25 per barrel from $20.
The company also lifted its organic capital expenditure forecast by €100 million to €3.5 billion, partly to accelerate investment in Romania's Neptun Deep gas project. Full-year hydrocarbon production is now expected to average around 290,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

title: IMI raises guidance after solid third quarter performance
full_text:
Investing.com -- IMI on Thursday reported organic constant currency sales growth of 2% in the third quarter of 2026, meeting analyst expectations despite facing tough year-over-year comparisons from the prior period’s 12% growth.
The company lifted its full-year earnings per share guidance to a range of 137 pence to 143 pence, up from the previous forecast of 136 pence to 142 pence.
The adjustment reflects an additional contribution from Truflo Marine, whose disposal shifted to the fourth quarter from the third quarter, and stronger performance in the Transport division.
For the first nine months of 2026, organic constant currency sales increased 4% across the group.
The Automation segment posted organic constant currency sales decline of 3% in the third quarter. Process Automation orders rose 19% on an organic constant currency basis in the quarter, driven by a large U.S. liquefied natural gas order and progress in hydrogen projects. Process Automation sales fell 6% in the quarter but remained up 1% for the nine-month period.
Life Technology recorded organic constant currency sales growth of 11% in the third quarter. Climate Control sales jumped 13% in the quarter, supported by data centre shipment timing. Year-to-date data centre orders reached £25 million, compared with £9 million in the same period last year.
Transport sales climbed 19% on an organic constant currency basis in the third quarter as the truck market recovered. Management now expects Transport to deliver high single-digit organic constant currency sales growth for the full year, raised from the previous mid single-digit forecast.
The company maintained its target to deliver mid single-digit organic constant currency sales growth for fiscal year 2026.

title: Asian currencies mixed as dollar steadies after Fed hold, PCE eyed
full_text:
The U.S. dollar index slipped marginally to 102.17, after the greenback retreated from a two-week high following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference. The euro and the sterling traded little changed.
The USD/JPY pair fell marginally by 0.1% to 157.76, leaving the yen slightly firmer against the dollar. The Australian dollar traded at $0.7055, while the New Zealand dollar was at $0.5622.
Fed holds rates as PCE data takes focus
The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote on Wednesday, while upgrading its assessment of economic growth to describe activity as expanding at a strong pace.
The decision put further changes to borrowing costs on hold as policymakers await more evidence on inflation, with the next meeting coming after next week’s U.S. midterm elections.
Warsh expressed confidence that inflation could return to the Fed’s 2% target without significantly slowing economic growth or pushing unemployment higher. His press conference offered little clarity on whether another increase would come in December, prompting traders to reduce expectations for rate hikes in 2027.
Markets are still pricing in a 78% probability of a December rate hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
Investors now turn to September’s personal consumption expenditures price index, due later Thursday, for fresh clues on the outlook for rates.
Traders are also awaiting the ECB’s policy announcement later on Thursday, where it is widely expected to keep its deposit rate unchanged at 2.50%.
Kiwi stabilizes after RBNZ surprise, Aussie tracks inflation
The New Zealand dollar steadied at $0.5622, down 0.1%, after tumbling as much as 1.7% to around $0.5585 on Wednesday. The sharp decline followed the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s unexpected decision to keep its official cash rate at 2.75%, contrary to market expectations.
The Australian dollar traded at $0.7055, near a one-month high, after quarterly inflation data showed consumer prices rose 1.3% in the third quarter, accelerating from 0.6% in the previous quarter.
Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock told lawmakers the central bank would assess at next week’s policy meeting whether the four rate increases delivered this year would be sufficient to return inflation to target.
Regional moves were uneven. The USD/CNH pair and the USD/CNY pair were little changed. The USD/KRW pair dropped 0.6% to 1,333.51, indicating a stronger South Korean won.
Elsewhere, the USD/SGD pair traded flat, while the USD/INR pair rose marginally by 0.1% to 95.290 and the USD/THB pair gained 0.16% to 33.744. The USD/TWD pair rose 0.5% to 32.554, pointing to a weaker Taiwan dollar.

title: Technip Energies beats on EBITDA with record quarterly profit
full_text:
Investing.com -- Technip Energies BV (EPA:TE) on Thursday reported third-quarter results that exceeded expectations, with adjusted EBITDA reaching a company record as profitability recovered from earlier disruptions in the Middle East.
The engineering and technology company posted adjusted EBITDA of €172 million for the third quarter, representing a margin of 8.9% and beating analyst consensus of €148 million. The strong performance was driven by a recovery in Project Delivery margins to 7.0%, surpassing the 5.6% consensus estimate, while Technology, Products & Services achieved its highest-ever margin at 16.1%.
For the nine months ended September 30, revenue rose 3% YoY to €5.6 billion, while adjusted EBITDA declined 20% YoY to €385 million. The company confirmed all fiscal 2026 guidance.
Third-quarter adjusted net income of €89 million slightly missed the company consensus of €91 million. Project Delivery EBITDA reached €101 million with a 7.0% margin, while TPS EBITDA came in at €80 million with a 16.1% margin, both exceeding expectations.
"We delivered year-over-year revenue growth through disciplined execution and close coordination with our customers," said Arnaud Pieton, Chief Executive Officer. "As anticipated, profitability recovered from the second quarter low and we achieved our highest-ever quarterly EBITDA in the third quarter."
Order intake for the third quarter totaled €1.4 billion, representing a book-to-bill ratio of 0.7x and beating consensus of €1.1 billion. The company’s backlog stood at €24.5 billion at quarter-end, down 2% from the prior quarter but up 54% from December 31, 2025.
Adjusted net cash reached €3.55 billion, slightly below consensus of €3.71 billion but up 4% from the second quarter.
The company maintained its fiscal 2026 guidance, projecting Project Delivery revenue of €5.7 billion to €6.3 billion with EBITDA margin above 5%, and TPS revenue of €1.9 billion to €2.2 billion with EBITDA margin around 15%. At the midpoint, this implies total revenue of €8.05 billion and EBITDA of €538 million.

title: Bitcoin weakens to $80k as hawkish Fed, mixed tech earnings weigh
full_text:
Investing.com-- Bitcoin fell on Thursday, cutting short a brief rebound from the prior session as the Federal Reserve’s October meeting reinforced bets on more interest rate hikes by the central bank.
A batch of mixed technology earnings in the U.S. and Asia also hampered risk sentiment, with broader crypto prices retreating in tandem with Bitcoin.
The world’s largest crypto fell 0.9% to $80,133.1 by 02:14 ET (06:14 GMT).
Get more insights on Bitcoin and crypto markets by subscribing to InvestingPro
Crypto markets dithered after September quarter earnings from Google owner Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and memory chip giant Samsung Electronics Co Ltd (KS:005930) sparked deep losses in their respective shares, which in turn spilled over into broader markets.
The move provided negative cues for crypto, given that the sector tends to usually track tech stocks.
Fed holds rates, but markets see Dec hike as likely
The Fed left interest rates unchanged at 4.0% as widely expected on Wednesday evening, although two members of the central bank’s 12-member board called for a 25 basis point hike.
Speaking after the meeting, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to offer any clear forward guidance on the Fed’s plans, but did highlight resilience in the U.S. economy, especially in private spending and the labor market.
Warsh also reiterated his commitment to reaching the Fed’s 2% annual inflation target.
Markets viewed the Fed Chair’s comments as likely setting the stage for an interest rate hike in the coming months. CME Fedwatch showed markets pricing in a 79.8% chance for a 25 bps hike in December, up from 73.4% a week ago.
U.S. Treasury yields also briefly surged after the Fed’s meeting, with the 10-year yield now trading back above the closely watched 5% level.
Higher rates bode poorly for speculative, risk-heavy assets like crypto, given that they increase the opportunity cost of investing in the sector.

World no.2 crypto Ether fell 1.5% to $2,316.64, while XRP fell 2.2%.
Solana shed 1.7%, Cardano slid 3.6%, while BNB outperformed with a 1.3% gain.
Memecoins Dogecoin and $TRUMP fell 1.6% apiece.

title: Glencore copper output rises 3% YTD; guidance unchanged
full_text:
Investing.com -- Glencore said on Thursday third-quarter copper production rose 2% from the second quarter to 201,600 tonnes, and kept its full-year production guidance of 810,000 to 870,000 tonnes. It expects copper output toward the lower end of that range.
Copper production for the first nine months was 598,600 tonnes, up 3% from the same period of 2025. Adjusting for the closure of the Mount Isa copper mine and the sale of the Kidd mine in June, output was 12% higher, driven by higher mining rates and grades in Africa and better grades at Antamina. Weaker output at Antapaccay and Collahuasi partly offset those gains.
The company expects a pickup in the fourth quarter, mainly from higher grades and recoveries at Collahuasi. "We are pleased to report a strong third quarter production performance," Chief Executive Gary Nagle said, adding that key assets largely performed in line with expectations.
Cobalt output fell 20% from the second quarter to 3,500 tonnes, and was 52% lower for the nine months, reflecting the Democratic Republic of Congo’s cobalt export regime. Zinc fell 4% to 181,600 tonnes, and nickel rose 1% to 18,800 tonnes.
Steelmaking coal rose 14% to 8.0 million tonnes, and energy coal rose 8% to 26.5 million tonnes.
Glencore has been restarting its ferrochrome smelters, with Boshoek restarting in September and Wonderkop in October, lifting attributable ferrochrome output 29% from the second quarter.
For the rest of its guidance, Glencore kept all ranges and said it expects zinc and energy coal toward the upper end, steelmaking coal toward the lower end and nickel around the middle. It also said it expects full-year marketing-adjusted EBIT to exceed $5 billion.
